Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Independently write a character-change paragraph with two timed references and one comment on what has not changed. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Sample: original example using character on new material; names a specific word, source or choice and explains its effect.

Parent: Written model 2: Sample error: Claiming a character “became nice” with no scene support.. Correction: Strong answer: change specific;. Why it helps the audience is stated.

Parent: Likely misconception: Claiming a character “became nice” with no scene support. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating character on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with character, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Accept original work about character with a specific supporting detail. Reject copied model wording with no new material. / Accept a misconception, a correction, and a purpose-linked reason for character. Reject corrections that do not change the inaccurate idea..

teach_steps.explain:
Characters change (or resist change) under pressure. Analysts track motivation, turning points and what remains stable, always with evidence.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.

Read the original example and locate the words or actions that support the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided.
